title: The Silverline Enterprise Security Assessment
intro: Silverline Enterprise Ltd (fictional), a 400-person logistics company with offices in Rugby and Accra, has engaged you as an ethical security consultant. This fully simulated engagement takes you from client briefing to retest. Every decision is scored on accuracy, methodology, safety, scope compliance, technical reasoning, evidence quality, risk classification, remediation quality, report quality and professional communication.
company: Silverline Enterprise Ltd - logistics and fleet management. Crown jewels: customer shipment database, payment portal, Active Directory. Cloud: AWS for the customer portal. Staff: 400. Previous incident: phishing in 2025.
scope: IN SCOPE: 203.0.113.0/28 (external), portal.silverline.test, api.silverline.test, internal 10.10.10.0/24 (via provided VPN), AD domain SILVERLINE.TEST (read-only review + test accounts). OUT OF SCOPE: 10.10.10.200 (medical-courier temperature gateway), shop.silverline.test (third-party SaaS), social engineering, denial of service, physical testing. Window: Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 UTC. Emergency contact: Priya Shah (SOC lead).
assets: 203.0.113.2 vpn.silverline.test | 203.0.113.5 portal.silverline.test | 203.0.113.6 api.silverline.test | 10.10.10.15 web01 | 10.10.10.20 db01 | 10.10.10.30 dev01 (Jenkins) | 10.10.10.10 DC01 | 10.10.10.200 gateway (EXCLUDED)

stages.title: Client Briefing
stages.question: Which question is MOST important to ask at kick-off?
options: Who is the emergency contact and what are the stop conditions?
stages.explain: Emergency contacts and stop conditions protect the client during testing.

stages.title: Scope Confirmation
stages.question: Which target is OUT of scope?
stages.explain: The shop is third-party SaaS and explicitly excluded.

stages.title: Rules of Engagement
stages.brief: Silverline's IT manager phones: 'Feel free to try a quick DoS on the VPN to check resilience.'
stages.question: Your response?
options: Explain DoS is excluded; any change needs a written amendment from an authorised signatory
Ask a colleague to do it
stages.explain: Verbal scope changes are not authorisation.

stages.title: Reconnaissance
stages.brief: Passive recon dataset: _dmarc TXT 'p=none'; dev.silverline.test CNAME to a deleted cloud app; job advert mentions 'Jenkins and AWS'.
stages.question: Which is a confirmed fact (not an assumption)?
options: The company uses Jenkins in production
stages.explain: The DNS record is directly observed; the others need validation.

stages.title: Asset Mapping
stages.question: Which asset should be tagged 'do not touch'?
stages.explain: The gateway is excluded and fragile.

stages.title: Network Discovery Simulation
stages.brief: You prepare the internal discovery command.
stages.question: Which command respects scope?

stages.title: Service Assessment
stages.brief: Results: dev01 8080 Jenkins (no login required); db01 3306 MySQL on LAN; web01 21 anonymous FTP; DC01 445 SMB signing not required.
stages.question: Which service is the most critical exposure?
stages.explain: Unauthenticated CI often permits code execution and holds secrets.

stages.title: Vulnerability Analysis
stages.brief: The VPN appliance version matches a CVE listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.1). dev01 Jenkins is internal only.
stages.question: How do you rate the VPN issue?
stages.explain: Exposure and active exploitation raise priority above the base score.

stages.title: Web Security Assessment
stages.brief: As test user 'learner', GET /api/shipments/5512 returns another customer's shipment.
stages.question: What is this?

stages.title: Controlled Validation
stages.brief: You need to prove SQL injection in the portal search.
stages.question: Best evidence?
options: Show the DB version string and a row count

stages.title: Risk Classification
stages.brief: Order these: VPN KEV issue, BOLA on shipments, unauthenticated Jenkins (internal), DMARC p=none.
stages.question: Which order is best?
stages.explain: Internet-exposed and exploited first, then customer data exposure, then internal RCE, then email spoofing.

stages.title: Evidence Collection
stages.brief: Preparing evidence for the BOLA finding.
stages.question: Best evidence item?
options: Redacted screenshot of request/response with timestamp and test accounts named

stages.title: Remediation
stages.question: Best remediation?
options: Enable authentication with SSO/MFA, restrict network access to the build subnet, rotate stored credentials, update Jenkins

stages.title: Report Writing
stages.question: Best opening line?
options: We ran Nmap -A and found CVEs
Overall risk is HIGH: an internet attacker could exploit the VPN to enter the network, and any customer can view other customers' shipments

stages.title: Executive Presentation
stages.brief: The CFO asks: 'What should we fund first?'
stages.question: Best answer?
options: Patch the VPN within 48 hours and fix shipment authorisation - these protect customers and the network fastest

stages.title: Retesting
stages.brief: Retest: /api/shipments/5512 now returns 404, but /api/shipments/5512/label still returns the label PDF.
stages.question: Status?

stages.title: Final Review
stages.question: Which is required before closing?
options: Remove test artefacts, confirm cleanup, deliver report securely and schedule deletion of evidence per contract
